column1: # Shared classification fixtures: command <TAB> expected-kind <TAB> expected-subject
# Two consumers read this file, and they must agree on every row:
#   - plugin/hooks/first-read-hint.sh --classify   (POSIX sh, runs in the hook)
# They are separate implementations because the hook must not require python at
# runtime and the analyser must not shell out per line. Separate implementations
# drift, so the drift is what this file tests. A measurement that counted a
# different set of commands than the hint fires on would answer a question
# expected-kind is one of: ident, file, none
# expected-subject is the identifier or path, and is empty for none.
# ── Identifier searches: a structural tool answers these ──────────────────────
# ── Text searches: grep is the right instrument, stay silent ─────────────────
grep -rn "chat-recall is not logged in. Run" .
# ── Source files printed whole: an outline is cheaper ────────────────────────
# ── Not source, or not a structural question ─────────────────────────────────
# ── Compound lines: the shape the agent actually runs ────────────────────────
# The verb is rarely the first word. With auto mode active the harness asks for
# absolute paths and routes file work through Bash, so a line arrives as
# `cd /repo; …` or `echo "=== x ==="; …`. Reading only the first command found
# `cd` where it wanted a verb and gave up: on one real session that was 25 Bash
# calls, 0 hints, 6 owed, and the first miss was the session's first tool call.
cd /repo; echo "=== upload path ==="; sed -n '690,740p' packages/cli/src/sync-client.ts
# ── Compound lines that are still not code questions ────────────────────────
export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/x.yaml; kubectl get deploy chat-recall
# ── Pipes and inverted matches: not questions about the code ─────────────────
# A grep after a pipe filters what the previous command printed, so it has no
# target because its input is not the tree. `… | grep -v test` was read as a
# search for `test` and hinted on it. Noise teaches the agent to skip the hint.
cd /repo; echo "=== caps ==="; grep -rn capabilities --include=*.ts packages/server/src 2>/dev/null | grep -v test | head -10
